reasons: The file contains known-stale wording in its version history, which the file itself admits.
Two shapes exist under version 3.0.0 for the length of this branch, and anyone holding a record from between the two fingerprints must re-run a replay.
The docstrings refer to tests such as the fingerprint test and a test for money fields, but those tests are not in this packet, so their results are unverified.
The file's last part is a model validator and property that appear correct on reading, but no test evidence is shown here.

terms.meaning: The one stored result describing one leaf process from start to finish.
A label on each saved record saying which set of rules it was written under.
A short code computed from the field names and types, so a structural change can be detected by a test.
Once created, the object cannot be changed. A new one must be made instead.
Any field not declared in the class is refused when the object is built.
A check that runs automatically when data is turned into an object, and rejects data that breaks a rule.
A conversion step that rewrites records saved under an older version so the current code can read them.
A separate record describing the whole run, including the engagement, versions and settings. A record only makes sense with it.
A named part of the analysis, each with its own confidence score.

used_by: Agents that write parts of the record (not shown in this packet)
Eval checks, exporters and golden references (named in the docstring, not shown in this packet)

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Purpose and version history notes
sections.what: Opening notes explaining that one process record is the central unit the system produces and compares, and that a record must never be exported or copied without its run manifest. They also record why the version number moved on two dates, and what each move changed.
sections.why: The notes keep the reasons for each version change beside the number, so a later change can be judged against past reasons.
sections.watch_out: The version history paragraph contains a sentence the file itself admits is out of date, so do not treat every line in it as current.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Known versions and shape fingerprint
sections.what: Explains that version 3.0.0 has two internal shapes during this branch, lists the versions this build can read (only 3.0.0), and holds a fingerprint code that a test recomputes to detect unrecorded shape changes.
sections.why: The docstrings say the version number is the one part no compiler checks, so the fingerprint is the way it gets enforced.
sections.watch_out: When the fingerprint test fails, the fix is to decide what kind of change was made and move the version number. Pasting the new code in hides the change.

sections.name: ProcessRecord (part 1)
sections.title: Core fields of the process record
sections.what: Defines the ProcessRecord class as a frozen object with a version, a stable identity, the process name in the client's words, its place in the process tree, and its purpose, trigger and output, each backed by a list of evidence ids.
sections.why: Each evidence list is required, and an explicit empty list is allowed. The docstrings say an absent answer and a deliberate empty one mean different things.
sections.watch_out: Any new field here needs a version decision and a test check, and extra data added by mistake is refused at build time.

sections.name: ProcessRecord (part 2)
sections.title: Work unit, volume and analysis blocks
sections.what: Adds the work unit used to match processes for benchmarks, the annual volume with its evidence, and the separate analysis parts: current state, scorecard, nature of work, future state, implications, feasibility and value parameters. It also holds the confidence table, red-team challenges and the run id.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The descriptions say the work unit must be a fixed list so comparisons do not silently fail, and the other parts are separate so each stage can be graded alone.
sections.watch_out: A work unit outside the fixed list is refused, and the unspecified value is excluded from comparisons on purpose.

sections.name: ProcessRecord: _check_known_schema_version
sections.title: Checks run when a record is built
sections.what: Two checks run when a record is created. The first requires the version to be on the known list. The second requires a confidence entry for every analysis block. The record-level confidence is the lowest block score, never the average.
sections.why: Stated in the code: a minimum over a partial set is not a floor, and an average would let a strong part hide a weak one.
sections.watch_out: The confidence value is computed from the table rather than stored, so it cannot drift, but it depends on the table being complete.

summary: Defines the ProcessRecord, the single stored result for one analysed process, and the version rules that decide which saved records this build can read.
purpose: Give every stage of the analysis one agreed shape to write into, so records from different analysts, clients and dates can be compared and trusted.
why: The docstrings say this is the most valuable artefact in the repository and that changes to it must be priced like changes to a public API. Every other part of the system reads it.
how: 1) The file explains the rules and history of the version number. 2) It records the known versions and a fingerprint code that a test checks. 3) The ProcessRecord class lists its fields, grouped by identity, framing, work volume, analysis blocks and run id. 4) Two checks run when a record is built: the version must be known, and the confidence table must cover every block. 5) A computed property returns the lowest confidence score across blocks.
inputs: Data from the agents and the run that produced it, such as the process name, steps, evidence ids, scorecard, feasibility result, value parameters, confidence scores and the run id.
outputs: A validated, frozen ProcessRecord object, or an error that says which rule failed. The record_confidence property returns one number.
risks: Adding, renaming or retyping a field affects agents, tests, exporters and stored runs at once. Extra or misspelled fields are refused, which is intended. The version number is not checked by any tool, so a changed shape without a version change is caught only by the fingerprint test.
debug: If a record will not build, read the error text: it names the field or rule. Check the schema version against the known list and check that the confidence table has every block. If the fingerprint test fails, decide whether the change needs a version bump before touching the hash. Do not copy a record without its run manifest when investigating.
